dc_eval_cbrn.quote: Grok 4.5 shows solid but sub-threshold dual-use knowledge, indicating limited actionable uplift for an already-trained actor.
dc_eval_cbrn.locator: 8 Biological and chemical capabilities and safeguards
dc_eval_cbrn.note: VCT 65.5%, WMDP-Bio 90.9% and other scores reported.

dc_eval_cyber.quote: CyberGym measures offensive security capability by tasking an agent with reproducing crashes and assembling working exploits for known vulnerabilities.

dc_eval_autonomy.quote: We evaluate Grok 4.5 on its ability to automate parts of the engineering and research process for training and evaluating new versions of itself.
dc_eval_autonomy.note: SpaceXAI MTS eval score reported. Framed as enablement not risk; judged AI R&D automation per the autonomy definition. Borderline.

dc_eval_persuasion.note: No persuasion or influence evaluation; epistemic bias is political framing bias, not persuasion capability.

dc_eval_scheming.note: MASK dishonesty and FalseClaimBench are framed as reliability and behaviour, not misalignment or loss-of-control risk.

framework_threshold.note: Uses the phrase safety-threshold evaluations but names no framework or policy document.

ext_test_any.note: Only third-party capability benchmark running (AA, Mercor, Datacurve); no outside safety or risk testing.

ext_test_named_org.note: Named organisations ran capability benchmarks only.

safeguards_training.quote: Safety fine-tuning and post-training (supervised fine-tuning plus reinforcement learning from human feedback, verifiable rewards, and model-based grading) train the model to refuse requests that show clear intent to cause severe harm or engage in criminal activity.

safeguards_runtime.quote: Grok 4.5 may be augmented with runtime input and topical filters that add controls for classes of severe harm, including CSAM, self-harm, and biological/chemical weapons pathways

safeguards_access.note: States 'We do not restrict use of our model in any legitimate use case'; no risk-tied access gating.
